title: The Lease in Kitengela and the Urinals Penda Health Had Removed
conflicts: Founders: the slate's 'Stephanie Weber' is not supported anywhere; Penda's own blog, VC4A and NextBillion name the three co-founders as Stephanie Koczela, Nick (Nicholas) Sowden and Beatrice Ngoche (VC4A once spells 'Kozcela'). Opening: planned for 30 January 2012, NextBillion says January, Koczela told VC4A February; story uses February 2012. Social Shares interest: 10% a year (Sowden's blog) vs 5% (NextBillion); story says 'with interest'. Money needed: about $13,000 projected (Sowden) vs $20,000 per clinic (NextBillion); story uses the founder's projection. Consultation fee: planned 200 shillings (Jan 2012 blog), Sh150 reported in Dec 2012; story gives only the plan. Distance from Nairobi half an hour (VC4A) vs an hour (NextBillion); VC4A used.
notes: The main source is Penda's own 2011-2012 Blogger site, used through the Internet Archive snapshot of its homepage of 11 February 2012, which carries Sowden's seed-funding story and update and Koczela's clinic-site and pricing posts; the individual posts were never archived separately. Dr Job Makoyo appears in a February 2012 VC4A team list but not as a co-founder; a Kenya Times profile naming a 'Jonathan Petrides' as co-founder was not used. Funding set to 'mixed' rather than the slate's 'venture'.
